newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 26.

text.p: The following are the highlights
of stories from the Irish press on Monday.
IRISH TIMES
- North Korea slides into chaos as infrastructure of daily life
disintegrates.
- The left causes an upset in first round of French elections.
- Cracks in Fianna Fail's campaign to form an alternative coalition with the Progressive Democrats may resurface today as FF publishes its policy document on public services.
- Over 1,000 jobs will be created in a 400-500 million Irish pound investment by the high-tech hard disk manufacturing firm
Seagate Technologies in Cork.
- Milk quotas and prices are topping the agenda for EU farm ministers holding three days of talks in Holland.
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- Ireland's 'black economy' now accounts for 15 percent of the national wealth and costs the Exchequer almost two billion Irish pounds a year in lost revenue

- Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats have held a crisis meeting at the midway point of the election campaign amid fears that the government coalition could yet overtake them. - The growth in the number of new hotel rooms in Dublin has kept accomodation prices at keener levels than elsewhere in Europe, a new index says.
THE EXAMINER
- Irish police stepped up security measures at the weekend
ahead of next week's election after the discovery of a bomb in
Dundalk.
British share values may be heading for a setback as rising bond
yields and fears of higher interest rate weigh on sentiment,
strategists say.
